summary: This bill amends the Clean Air Act to double the penalty for each rate increase an investor-owned electric or gas utility imposes in the 2 years before or after a noncompliance penalty assessment.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Clean Air Act to enhance civil penalties assessed against noncompliant investor-owned utilities. It does not authorize, appropriate, or alter any federal spending, outlays, or budgets.
The legislation modifies penalty calculations under the Clean Air Act; these are regulatory fines, not taxes. No provisions change tax rates, credits, deductions, or tax policy.
No provisions address health insurance, medical care delivery, public health programs, or market-based versus government healthcare structures.
The bill contains no references to firearms, background checks, restrictions, or Second Amendment protections.
No content relates to immigration pathways, border enforcement, visas, asylum, or related protections or restrictions.
The legislation does not address reproductive health services, abortion access, funding, or restrictions.
No provisions concern military budgets, defense procurement, troop levels, or national security spending.

The bill directly amends Section 120(b) of the Clean Air Act to increase penalties on noncompliant electric or gas utilities that raise consumer rates near the time of a violation assessment. This strengthens enforcement of existing air-pollution standards and raises the financial cost of noncompliance, thereby supporting stronger environmental regulation and protection.
No provisions modify eligibility, funding, or administration of welfare programs, SNAP, housing assistance, or other safety-net benefits.
The bill does not address schools, federal education funding, school choice, or privatization.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, enforcement priorities, or drug-related sentencing.
The changes affect civil/administrative penalties under environmental law, not criminal sentencing, policing practices, or rehabilitation programs.
No provisions involve tariffs, trade agreements, import/export rules, or protectionist measures.
While enhanced penalties could marginally increase federal receipts, the bill does not address deficit levels, debt ceilings, or fiscal policy priorities.
No content pertains to legal protections, nondiscrimination rules, or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The legislation contains no provisions on foreign assistance, international aid programs, or related funding.
No references to voting access, election administration, voter ID, or campaign finance.
The bill does not address data privacy, technology regulation, surveillance, or platform liability.
No provisions concern collective bargaining, union rights, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
The legislation does not engage with religious exemptions, civil-rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and antidiscrimination rules.
